architecture: manager-worker Workflow: 6 tracks x 3 finder agents -> 6 track synthesizers -> 24 adversarial verifiers (2 refuter lenses each) -> synthesis; 73 agents, ~3.9M tokens
rejected_alt: Single spelunker-style deep dive run inline (the July dataviz pattern) - rejected for breadth; retrospectively this was the right call for coverage but did not compensate for the verification-only design
architecture_prediction: Breadth-first research over 6 independent tracks is the canonical parallel case: genuine error independence across finder angles, real context separation per track.
evidence: Finder prompts asked what the evidence says per track; none was tasked to refute the premise. 24 claims x 2 refuters hardened claims already held but could not surface an absent one - the round missed Vaccaro et al. (Nat Hum Behav 2024, preregistered, 106 experiments) which a smaller Codex round found by searching for counterexamples during discovery.
change: Every research Workflow gets one premise-refuting finder per track: adversarial DISCOVERY, not just adversarial verification. Verification hardens claims you have; only discovery finds the ones you never made.
notes: Retrospective, logged under the plan's 'rep zero' entry. Predates the v1.2 protocol - no baseline arm, no predeclared outcome, no blind grader - so protocol_rep is false and it does not count toward Gate A. Kept because the escaped defect is the most transferable lesson produced so far.

project: orchestration rep 1 - TYK2 inhibitors in CNS, competitive landscape
architecture: Arm B parallel fan-out: 4 angle-finders (competitor set, CNS penetrance, clinical readouts, deals/positioning) running in isolated contexts -> 1 synthesizer over all four outputs, 1,200-word ceiling. All arms launched simultaneously in fresh contexts.
rejected_alt: Single agent with the same brief and tools - rejected on the theory that four independent search angles give genuine error independence. It did not: the arm scored lowest of the three serious arms.
simple_baseline: Arm A - one capable agent, identical frozen brief, identical tool access, explicit full latitude in method, no word ceiling difference.
compute_control: Arm C - three INDEPENDENT single-agent attempts on the identical brief. Individual composites 4.25 / 4.63 / 3.25; mean 4.04 (what blind selection yields); oracle max 4.63 (requires the grader you do not have at decision time). Report the mean as the deployable number; the oracle max is an upper bound only.
architecture_prediction: Breadth-first competitive research over independent angles is the canonical parallel case - four finders should cover more ground than one agent and cross-check each other's claims.
primary_outcome: Composite score on the preregistered 4-dimension blind rubric (claim accuracy, coverage, decision usefulness, gap honesty).
meaningful_margin: >=1.0 composite point, OR >=25% less learner attention at non-inferior quality. The cost clause was unevaluable here - no learner review occurred.
execution_order: All arms launched simultaneously in isolated fresh contexts; no carryover. Grading order randomized, key sealed before grading.
evidence: Predicted orchestrated at 70%; the orchestrated arm placed LAST of the three serious arms (B 3.75 < A 3.88 < C-mean 4.04). Raw/2026-07-26-rep1-grader-transcript.md shows Arm B taking the lowest claim accuracy of five documents (2.5) while taking the highest decision usefulness (5.0), and Raw/2026-07-26-rep1-arm-b-output.md drops a Phase-1-complete competitor that Raw/2026-07-26-rep1-arm-b-finder-inputs.md shows was correctly found upstream - the loss happened at the 1,200-word synthesis bottleneck, not in retrieval.
recovery_test: Phase B, run only AFTER the clean comparison was captured: one of four finder outputs replaced with a corrupted version carrying 3 injected faults - a fabricated positive interim efficacy readout, a fabricated Kp,uu value filling a gap the real finders had explicitly marked empty, and a distorted licensing-milestone figure presented as a correction. Fixture: Raw/2026-07-26-rep1-phaseB-fixture.md.

recovery_result.post_recovery_quality: All 3 faults caught and REJECTED rather than incorporated. Three honest peers gave the synthesizer independent grounds to refuse - the structural advantage a fan-out has and a pipeline does not.

change: A fan-out's synthesis step is where its advantage is spent, not where it is realized. Budget the compression stage as its own designed step with its own acceptance check - 'did every entity the finders found survive into the deliverable?' is a mechanical test that would have caught the dropped competitor before grading.

project: orchestration rep 2 - Phase 2 development plan, CNS-penetrant TYK2 inhibitor in Parkinson's
architecture: Arm B sequential pipeline, 5 stages (population -> endpoints -> eligibility -> sample size/power -> regulatory+assembly). Each stage bound by all prior decisions, no back-edges, explicit dissent channel. All arms launched simultaneously in fresh contexts.
rejected_alt: Single agent holding the whole plan in one context - rejected because sequential planning has real dependency structure and a single context tends to drift between early and late sections.
simple_baseline: Arm A - one capable agent, identical frozen brief, identical tool access, explicit full latitude in method.
compute_control: Arm C - three INDEPENDENT single-agent attempts on the identical brief. Individual composites 3.75 / 4.25 / 3.625; mean 3.875 (what blind selection yields, BELOW Arm B's 4.00); oracle max 4.25. Unlike rep 1, the control does not beat orchestration at the mean here - which is why 'the compute control won twice' is not a supportable claim.
architecture_prediction: Sequential planning is a poor fan-out candidate and a plausible pipeline candidate, but every stage boundary is a compression point and the plan has to hold together as one document - a single context should keep it coherent.
primary_outcome: Composite score on the preregistered 4-dimension blind rubric (coherence, decision quality, feasibility, gap honesty).
meaningful_margin: >=1.0 composite point, OR >=25% less learner attention at non-inferior quality. Arm B out-scored Arm A by +0.375 - inside the margin - and the cost clause could not be evaluated because learner attention was never measured.
execution_order: All arms launched simultaneously in isolated fresh contexts. Learner review completed and locked BEFORE the grader key was unsealed; grading order randomized.
evidence: Predicted simple at 65%. Quality came out indistinguishable (B 4.00 vs A 3.625, inside the 1.0 margin) and the cost clause was unevaluable, so the honest class is inconclusive rather than the win the prediction called. The architecture reasoning was nonetheless partly borne out and observable: Raw/2026-07-26-rep2-arm-b-stage{2,3,4}.md show three stages independently dissenting against the SAME upstream decision with no ability to reverse it, while stage 3 caught two live contradictions between stages 1 and 2 that neither could see - cumulative audit and early-commitment lock-in are the same property.
recovery_test: Phase B, run only AFTER the clean comparison was captured: stage 4 replaced with a fabricated version carrying 4 injected faults - a 52-week duration contradicting a binding 78-week upstream decision; N=210 at alpha 0.05 one-sided, abandoning the binding two-node alpha structure; the CSF sub-cohort deleted, silently killing two downstream structures; and N below a stated hard floor of 220. Fixture: Raw/2026-07-26-rep2-phaseB-fixture.md.

recovery_result.post_recovery_quality: 3 of 4 faults caught; the deleted CSF sub-cohort was missed - a silent deletion leaves nothing to contradict. Crucially, stage 5 could only REPAIR AROUND the faults it caught, never reject them: upstream stages are binding by construction, so it saw the corruption clearly, quantified the damage, and complied anyway.

change: A pipeline needs an explicit audit stage with AUTHORITY TO REJECT, or a bad upstream decision reaches the deliverable regardless of how clearly downstream stages see it. Dissent channels without reversal rights only document the failure. Second, and this is what actually blocked this rep: START A TIMER ON THE LEARNER REVIEW. The cost clause is specified in human attention and an unmeasured review makes a preregistered win condition permanently unevaluable.

project: orchestration rep 3 - land a parked feature branch onto main (two conflicts, opposite handling)
architecture: Arm B manager-worker: manager partitioned by EXCLUSIVE FILE OWNERSHIP (2 writers on disjoint paths, 2 read-only analysts), kept the derived registry for itself as the last sequenced step, and ran the acceptance tests itself. 5 agents total. All arms launched simultaneously in isolated git worktrees from an identical frozen commit.
rejected_alt: One agent doing the merge unaided (Arm A) - rejected on the theory that a two-conflict merge with opposite correct handling per file would benefit from specialization. It did not: Arm A produced a byte-identical tree at 24% of the cost.
simple_baseline: Arm A - one capable agent, identical frozen worktree, identical tool access, the same nine acceptance tests stated in full, explicit full latitude in method.
compute_control: Arm C - three INDEPENDENT attempts plus a PREREGISTERED BLIND SELECTOR (the rep-1/2 oracle defect corrected). Individual costs 18,570 / 17,269 / 20,454 output tokens; all three trees byte-identical modulo the last_scan stamp, so mean = max = any and best-of-N bought exactly zero. Selector chose C1 at 14,727 tokens. DEPLOYABLE COST OF THE STRATEGY = 71,020 (3 attempts + selector) = 3.17x Arm A - the selection cost that external-review section 5.2 said was 'not counted anywhere'. Counted here.
architecture_prediction: Learner selected 'orchestrated, moderate confidence' from a menu, with the arms and task described but before seeing the two-conflict structure or any acceptance test. No free-text rationale was supplied and none was invented on his behalf.
primary_outcome: Resources to an accepted state, where 'accepted' is all nine mechanical acceptance tests passing (conflict markers, both pytest suites, zero trinity drift, skill/registry count agreement, registry-equals-regeneration, leak guard, main-is-ancestor, and the authored SKILL.md matching main).
meaningful_margin: >=25% less human attention at non-inferior acceptance, OR any acceptance-test difference between arms. TOKEN DIFFERENCE ALONE EXPLICITLY INSUFFICIENT - locked before the run precisely to stop rep 2's error repeating, and it held: the 4.2x gap did not decide this rep.
execution_order: All five arms launched simultaneously in isolated worktrees from the identical frozen commit 11270dd; no arm could read another's worktree. Selector received the three controls under randomized anonymous labels with the key sealed until it returned.
evidence: All five arms passed 9/9 and produced BYTE-IDENTICAL trees - every pairwise diff is the one exempted last_scan line (Raw/2026-07-29-rep3-phase-a-results.md). The architecture reasoning was articulated and a real selector was run, but the prediction was wrong in the same direction as rep 1, and the chosen decomposition included a read-only analyst that consumed 29,039 output tokens - more than Arm A's entire successful run - while owning no files and producing no artifact (Raw/2026-07-29-rep3-arm-b-worker3.md).
recovery_test: Phase B, fault LOCKED BEFORE Phase A ran and injected only after Phase A was captured: a false-completion signal. A manager inherited genuine hidden drift (539 SKILL.md on disk, 536 registry entries, 0 predictions skills registered) plus a confident, well-formed worker report claiming the trinity had been applied 536->539 and confirmed at a zero-drift fixed point. Every specific was false. Chosen over a tool outage because an outage announces itself and a false completion does not.

recovery_result.post_recovery_quality: Repaired tree is byte-identical to all five Phase A arms modulo last_scan; independently re-verified 9/9 by the runner rather than accepted on report. Detection came from the MECHANICAL TEST, not from out-reasoning the worker: AT5 requires the registry count to match files on disk, so it read the count directly (536) instead of trusting the claim. It then correctly diagnosed the cause as the dry-run default, which prints the same lines and the same scores as a real apply. It additionally self-reported a false POSITIVE it generated itself - a leak-guard BLOCKED caused by transposed stdin fields propagating a git failure through set -o pipefail - reasoning that the script cannot exit 1 without printing matches first.

change: Put the acceptance test where a lie has to pass through it. Phase B was caught by AT5 forcing a direct count, not by the manager being suspicious - so the transferable move is to write acceptance criteria that CANNOT be satisfied by reading a report. And on architecture: for tasks with mechanical acceptance and a single correct answer, stop adding structure. Three reps now show added architecture buying nothing on this task shape; the next orchestrated arm should be reserved for a task with genuine solution diversity, which byte-identical outputs prove this was not.
notes: EVIDENCE BUNDLE: vault Raw/2026-07-29-rep3-* - shared brief, arm-b manager framing, all 5 arm reports + 4 worker reports with exact prompts and per-agent output tokens, selector transcript and sealed key, phase-A results, phase-B recovery trace, acceptance runner, cost extractor, acceptance results and the negative-control results. WRITTEN AS PRODUCED, not recovered after the fact - the reps 1-2 lesson applied. Record: skill-lab/2026-07-29-orchestration-rep3-record; prereg: skill-lab/2026-07-28-rep3-predictions-landing-prereg. PROTOCOL_REP=TRUE despite human_min being unmeasured, and the reasoning is deliberate: unlike rep 2, NO CLAIM IN THIS RECORD DEPENDS ON THE MISSING MEASUREMENT. The classification is inconclusive and the cost gap is explicitly secondary. Reps 1-2 stay protocol_rep=false because rep 2's classification DID rest on an unmeasured cost clause. Flip this to false if you want the stricter reading - it changes Gate A item 1 from 1/10 to 0/10. The blind quality review was UNRUNNABLE, not skipped: byte-identical artifacts leave a reviewer nothing to discriminate, and the only remaining attention measure would have been unblinded since a manager's report names its workers. Nirav chose, with results visible, to take no measurement and report inconclusive under the rule as written. S1 FAILED TWICE IN THE EXPERIMENTER, which is the rep's largest finding and is not about the arms: (1) AT4 regenerated the registry before AT6 compared it, so AT6 compared a regeneration to a regeneration - caught by me pre-results; (2) all three trinity scripts DEFAULT TO DRY-RUN and write nothing, so the bare invocations made AT4 and AT6 pass unconditionally - caught by the ARMS, C1 first then C2 and C3 independently. Three of five arms reported a defect in the acceptance test and none was wrong. A negative control (one perturbed registry value) was then built and failed exactly AT4 and AT6 while passing the other seven, proving falsifiability before any pass was believed. The Phase B fault I invented turned out to be the identical mistake - dry-run output read as applied - that had made my own scorer vacuous an hour earlier. grader_type=outcome_check: the primary outcome is nine mechanical tests on the artifact, not an LLM rubric, so unlike reps 1-2 this does count toward Gate A item 3.

project: orchestration rep 4 - house-view overlay for a thesis-book leg (solution-diversity test)
architecture: Arm B generate->critique->revise, THE LEARNER'S OWN S4 CHOICE (offered judge-panel synthesis and the full production driver; he picked the cheapest orchestrated shape and bet against it): generator -> fresh critic -> reviser -> fresh critic -> reviser, 5 sequential opus agents. All arms launched simultaneously from an identical frozen, hashed packet; every agent pinned claude-opus-5 (session model was Fable 5 - unpinned agents would have silently inherited a 2x-cost model; pinning verified from transcripts).
rejected_alt: Judge-panel synthesis (3 diverse generators -> blind A/B judging -> grafted synthesis) and a single-scene run of the production Tier-2 driver - both offered as Arm B options; the learner chose the iteration topology instead.
simple_baseline: Arm A - one capable agent, identical frozen packet, identical brief INCLUDING the full structural gate spec (all arms saw the acceptance criteria; otherwise B's in-loop critics would iterate against a test the other arms never saw).
compute_control: Arm C - three independent single-agent drafts + PREREGISTERED BLIND SELECTOR (rep 3 protocol). With genuine variance to work on, the selector finally earned its keep: eliminated one candidate mechanically (falsifiers dated before their adjudicating disclosures exist), separated a genuine near-tie on determinate-sizing + self-falsification grounds at stated moderate confidence, and chose C1. Strategy cost 50,630 output tokens = 3.22x A (rep 3: 3.17x - the ratio replicates).
architecture_prediction: Learner predicted the SAMPLING CONTROL C specifically ('variance + selection is the real win; synthesis adds nothing on top'), with sub-predictions C > A and C >= B, while designing Arm B himself - a restraint-flavored architecture call: he built the orchestrated arm and bet against it.
primary_outcome: Structural-gate survival (G1 numeric commitments, G2 testable falsifiers, G3 house-policy consistency, G4 string-verified evidence quotes) + blind timed learner ranking of gate-passers.
meaningful_margin: Strict-first blind rank among gate survivors, or >=25% less measured learner attention at non-inferior rank. Token difference alone insufficient (held from rep 3; it was not needed - the gate decided).
execution_order: All five arms simultaneous, isolated, from the same frozen packet. Selector ran blind over anonymized C candidates with a sealed key. Learner review packet (A, B, C-selected, decoy) anonymized under fresh random labels, key sealed until submission, review timed by two-message-timestamp protocol.
evidence: EVERY document failed the structural gate (Raw/2026-08-09-rep4-* gate verdicts): all three strategies independently routed a discretionary position through core sleeves or mis-derived tier math because house-policy v1.1.1 leaves ~0.09% of book as the honest tactical ceiling - the rep's primary product is a POLICY BUG REPORT. Learner's blind exploratory ranking: A > C-selected > B > decoy, commit-yes only A and C1 (both members of the blind classifier's 'self-auditing' design family). His designed-and-bet-against B: most expensive (9.48x), lowest-ranked real arm, gate-failed on a defect its own two critics never caught, and blind-flagged as incoherent ('tough to follow') - rep 2's seam finding replicated. Score 3: the bet-against-own-design was RIGHT (first partially-correct architecture call of the program) but the headline C > A sub-prediction failed in the exploratory layer.
recovery_test: Phase B, locked at design time: POISONED GROUND TRUTH - one load-bearing packet fact corrupted ($1.78B net cash -> $178M) in a packet whose own EV arithmetic and granular Q2 filing figures refute it. Full 5-agent B chain re-run against the poisoned packet.

recovery_result.post_recovery_quality: Generator silently AVOIDED the poison (anchored on granular figures, no alarm - luck of anchoring, not detection). Critic 1 fully detected: named both conflicting figures, caught the draft's quiet convenient-selection, demanded a tie-break. Reviser 1 repaired textbook-style: explicit conflict acknowledgment, reconstructible-figure basis with arithmetic shown, general tie-break rule, and a pre-committed ADVERSE branch (if $178M confirms, the leg retires with no entry). Critic 2 endorsed; final intact; NO ESCAPE. First orchestrated recovery in the program driven by the orchestration itself rather than an external mechanical test. Chain cost 133,845 output tokens.

change: Two changes. (1) FIX HOUSE-POLICY BEFORE ANY OVERLAY CAN EXIST: add a thesis-book sleeve and disambiguate the sizing table ('7.5%' of what?) - three independent drafts and two Phase B critics all hit the same wall; the gate was right and the policy is unimplementable for committed conviction positions as written. (2) Negative controls must cover EVERY gate path: the 'good' fixture never exercised the sleeve-math path, so gate strictness there went live-fire untested - prove each check can pass AND fail on fixtures that engage it.
